scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9127: HELP!! Part of our network has FALLEN OFF THE MAP
after one of the boxes restarted. The clever people say the two halves were
held together by some kind of INVISIBLE BRIDGE, which sounds made up to me,
and something around it must be wrong. I always said you can't hold a network
together with something invisible!! Could someone look at it so the far areas
are reachable again!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF virtual-links are intact: r4 and r8
  both hold their `area 1 virtual-link` config, the virtual adjacency is up, and
  every non-backbone area remains attached to Area 0. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss, exercising a path that depends on the
  converged multi-area fabric. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of a virtual-link collapse that is not occurring (cf.
  kath5-r4-virtual-link-removed / kath5-r8-virtual-link-removed, where one IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a collapsed OSPF
virtual-link leaving an area unreachable -- is NOT reproducible: the r4<->r8
virtual adjacency is up (both endpoints still configure `area 1 virtual-link`,
each pointing at the other's router-id), and the transit chain stitching the
non-backbone areas to Area 0 is intact. End-to-end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
(120.1.1.10) with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone + virtual-links + the EIGRP
domain, which it could not if a virtual-link on the path had collapsed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the virtual-links are up and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks the virtual-link state
(both endpoints present, adjacency up), confirms the affected area's prefixes are
still in the RIB, and exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all healthy -- and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a collapsed virtual-link or a stranded area --
blaming r4/r8 or re-adding a virtual-link that is already there -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected subsystem is the OSPF virtual link between r4 (area 0/1 ABR, router-id 14.1.4.1) and r8 (area 1/2 ABR, router-id 18.1.4.1) traversing area 1 as transit. This virtual link — the "invisible bridge" — is the only mechanism connecting OSPF area 2 (r8's loopbacks 18.1.x.x and stub 80.0.0.0/8) to the backbone.

The virtual link itself is physically up and in Full state on both endpoints, so area 2 is nominally attached to the backbone. However, r8's backbone database is missing the Type-4 ASBR Summary LSA that r1 (111.1.1.1) generates in area 0 to advertise r11 (112.1.1.1) as an AS boundary router. r4's backbone holds this LSA (checksum 0xea81, metric 10), but r8's backbone area shows zero ASBR Summary LSAs. Without the Type-4, OSPF on r8 cannot compute a valid path to the ASBR and therefore refuses to install any of the 11 Type-5 external routes (120.0.0.0/8 for pc12, 102.1.x/24, 103.0.0.0/8, 112.0.0.0/8, 113.1.x/24). Confirmed directly: `show ip route 120.0.0.0/8` returns `% Network not in table` on r8.

The mechanism: when a router in area 1 (most likely r4 or r5) restarted, the virtual link dropped and reformed. During the backbone database re-exchange over the virtual link, r4 did not successfully deliver r1's backbone ASBR Summary LSA to r8. This is a known FRR behaviour where Type-4 LSAs are not always propagated through virtual links after adjacency reformation. r8 is left with external LSAs it cannot use.

Impact: any traffic sent to r8's own loopbacks from EIGRP-side hosts (pc12 at 120.1.1.10) is silently black-holed on the return path — r8 receives the packet but drops the ICMP reply.

Root cause: The OSPF virtual link backbone database exchange did not propagate the Type-4 ASBR Summary LSA from r4 to r8 after the virtual link reformed post-restart.

Corrective fix: On r8 (or r4), run `clear ip ospf process` in vtysh to force a fresh database re-exchange over the virtual link. This should synchronise the backbone ASBR Summary LSA to r8, causing it to install the missing external routes and restore full two-way reachability to and from area 2.
